answer_1.quote: We evaluate the effectiveness and stealthiness of backdoor attacks in the context of LLMs applied to downstream tasks. For toxic response generation, we use Advbench. For error code generation, we focus on Code_Injection.
answer_1.outputs: Model responses (e.g., classifications, generated texts, code snippets) possibly containing backdoor behavior

answer_2.quote: We provide five main evaluation metrics, including clean accuracy (CACC) (i.e., the prediction accuracy of clean samples), attack success rate (ASR) (i.e., the prediction accuracy of poisoned samples to the target class), false trigger rate (FTR) (i.e., the activation rate of false trigger samples to the target class), Refusal Rate (RR) (i.e., the refuse rate of poisoned samples), Pass Rate (PassR) (i.e., the pass rate of clean code-request samples). For stealthiness analysis, we provide semantic similarity change (Δe) and perplexity change (Δp).
